newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil called $1-$1.50 up, IPE Brent steady.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil called $1-$1.50 up, IPE Brent steady.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures were expected to open $1-$1.50 higher on Tuesday to catch up with the Brent contract's gains at yesterday's close, brokers said.

Benchmark blend crude futures were predicted starting unchanged at around the settle of $18.51 after Monday's late break through resistance. August Brent gained 36 cents on Monday, mainly on further delays to Iraqi crude exports.

Gas oil closed at $162.25 and would begin strong to pull itself into line with crude, which was helped higher by short covering which pushed the front-month to a session high of $18.57 in the last half-hour.

"We had a quiet product expiry on the (NYMEX) gasoline and heat and once that was out of the way we saw some buying come in," said one broker. "But we are still trading on the same fundamentals from the weekend."
"We didn't see much volume so perhaps when it broke out of its range it was a reason for the shorts to cover."
The market's underlying strength was provided by comments made by Iraqi envoy Abdul Amir al-Anbari who said he did not anticipate Baghdad resuming crude flows until August.
"It would take about a month for the new resolution to be implemented, including the oil sales," Anbari said on Monday.
